admitted_claims: The exact-SHA producer rerun deterministically rebuilt all four M52 configurations byte-for-byte, and an independent record reconstruction matched 160 record rows, 40 per-sample aggregates, all nearest-rank percentiles, capacity arithmetic, complexity widths and gates with zero mismatch.

Changing the sole M45 context-capacity guard from 8 to 16 is mechanically isolated and semantically controlled for the frozen abstract transaction scheduler: its ready-selection window is 16, context occupancy is dynamically bounded by the parameter, and complete credits are reserved by actual group length.

K4-C16 passes the predeclared transaction and byte-capacity arithmetic gates and is sufficiently motivated for a new RTL/VCS/Synopsys experiment only; it is not an admission of K4 hardware feasibility or performance.

K8-C16 is killed under the frozen predeclared policy because its incremental integrated p95 gain over K4-C16 is 4.1454%, below 5%, while its source-only cycles regress by 0.8705% and its structural widths double again.

The exact conditional frozen-compute ratio is 3.081290603812283x, but its denominator includes a conservative non-address-timed pair upper bound and therefore is not a measured, full-network, end-to-end or system speedup.

context16_guard_extension.reason: The single guard edit is isolated and all four context-capacity uses remain parameterized, but the Python scheduler stores task identities in dynamic containers rather than exercising a finite 4-bit tag allocator, wrap/reuse, or response-tag implementation.

findings.finding: The reported maximum_metadata_occupancy is assigned from min(16, len(ready)); it is a clamped ready-window count, not an enqueue/dequeue occupancy ledger for the separately provisioned 16-entry response-metadata FIFO.
findings.impact: The boolean k4_ctx16_fifo_and_context_occupancy_within_capacity does not prove response FIFO feasibility or absence of response-queue backpressure. This does not invalidate the frozen abstract transaction replay or the decision to build an experiment, but it blocks treating all promotion gates as hardware-feasibility gates.
findings.required_repair: The K4 RTL experiment must expose response metadata enqueue/dequeue/occupancy and tag identity each cycle, prove occupancy <=16 under backpressure, and rerun cycle accounting if any new stall appears.

findings.finding: C16 uses dynamic Python task identities and scalar occupancy; no finite 4-bit context-ID allocator, free-list, tag wrap/reuse, or stale-response rejection is modeled.
findings.impact: The 8-to-16 guard change is controlled only at transaction-model level.
findings.recommended_followup: Implement and assert exact 4-bit context ownership and response-tag lifecycle in the K4-C16 RTL experiment.

findings.finding: K4 doubles the admitted K2 structural response work to 384 RMW paths, 3072 signed bank terms, four atomic vectors and 7296 payload bits excluding tags, without RTL, SRAM-port mapping, timing, area or power evidence.
findings.impact: The DSE can select K4 for an experiment, but cannot predict that the nominal cycle gain survives implementation.
findings.recommended_followup: Build exact-SHA K2-C16/K4-C16 VCS and Synopsys A/B with identical memory macros and include response arbitration stalls.

findings.finding: K4-C16 has 17040 bytes headroom, only 656 bytes above the predeclared 16-KiB gate; allocator/control state, macro banking and port replication are not physically itemized.
findings.impact: The arithmetic gate passes exactly, but configuration ranking is sensitive to costs outside the datapath-buffer ledger.
findings.recommended_followup: Freeze a field-level RTL state map and target SRAM macro organizations before treating capacity as implementation-ready.

findings.finding: K8 is eliminated by a frozen one-sequence heuristic and schedule: 4.1454% incremental p95 gain is below 5%, source cycles rise 0.8705%, and structural widths double versus K4.
findings.impact: The kill is valid for this search branch but is not proof that every K8 scheduler or workload is inferior.
findings.recommended_followup: Keep K8 out of RTL unless a materially different scheduler crosses the predeclared gate on broader sequences.

findings.finding: The 3.081290603812283x value combines frozen outside-block cycles with a conservative pair p95 that was not address-timed or replayed with shared-memory contention.
findings.impact: It is a conditional compute-model crossing only, not system or end-to-end performance.
findings.recommended_followup: Replace the composed denominator with address-timed full-network replay and measured RTL/SRAM timing before using any 3x headline.

findings.finding: Nearest-rank p95 over ten windows is the sample maximum, and all windows come from the same frozen sequence/cohort.
findings.impact: The deterministic tail comparison is exact for the cohort but supplies little cross-sequence generality.
findings.recommended_followup: Extend identical gates to multiple DSEC sequences and density/equal-rate strata without retuning thresholds.

not_admitted: Response-metadata FIFO event occupancy, K4 atomic-push4 correctness, finite C16 context-tag behavior, or absence of new RTL stalls.
K4/K8 RTL correctness, VCS cycles, Formality, Synopsys synthesized area/frequency/power/energy, SRAM macro port feasibility, or physical timing.
The K8 kill as a universal architectural conclusion outside the frozen scheduler, cohort and predeclared gates.
The conditional 3.081290603812283x ratio as address-timed, full-network, end-to-end, system, accelerator-comparison, DATE, or best-paper performance.
